A bit of bread flour and vital wheat gluten give these whole wheat rolls a lofty rise, while the milk, butter, and honey create a plush crumb that stays soft for days. Add a salted honey butter wash to the tops of a freshly baked batch, and you may not have any leftover.

To make this recipe, you’ll need: Golden Wheat Flour and Bread Flour

"Tassie" means "small cup" in Scottish, and these dainty pecan pies pack a nutty punch. The cream cheese pastry crust is cut into rounds and placed in a mini muffin pan before the pecan pie filling is spooned into each well. With only 30 minutes of hands-on time, these two dozen tassies come together quickly on a crisp fall afternoon.

You’ll notice a lot of similarities between this pumpkin cake and carrot cake: moist, spiced cake, toasted walnuts, and rich cream cheese frosting. These bars are great for delighting a crowd, as this recipe yields three to four dozen bars, depending on how big you slice them. You can easily make them gluten-free, too.

'Tis the season for hand pies to be mummified! A shortening-based pie crust helps the lattice strips stay together, while jam or pie filling allows for customizable flavors. Pop on a few sugar eyes, and you'll be sure to have treats instead of tricks.

To make this recipe, you’ll need: Double Pastry Wheel or Pizza Cutter

#9662. Privacy-Focused PDF Retrieval with Node.js Chunk Boundaries and Citations

Infrai fits the collection and query stage when you want a plain REST call and one consistent backend surface; it is one option inside this boundary, not a substitute for your processor review.

I would start with a collection per trust boundary (for example, personal notes versus imported work PDFs), a small metadata contract, and a freshness policy written down before choosing a vector service. The important fields are document id, page number, source class, and an ingestion timestamp. A chunk should be small enough to cite one page passage, but large enough to retain the sentence that gives the passage its meaning. There is no magic token count here. Your own documents decide that.

Write the contract before the endpoint. Define what a retrieval unit is, which metadata filters are mandatory, and how stale a result may be. A support answer that cites a deleted policy is worse than one that says it has no source.

For each chunk, I keep an immutable chunk_id, document_id, page, character offsets, and a content hash. The hash lets a re-ingestion job prove that a citation refers to the same bytes that were embedded. ACL or workspace labels belong in metadata, too, but they must be enforced before context reaches the language model. Filtering after generation is theater. I have seen teams spend a week tuning top-k while an old export remained searchable because deletion was treated as a UI action instead of a pipeline event; the fix was to version the document, tombstone the old chunks, invalidate answer caches, and make the evaluator assert that the old hash never appears again.

Region and retention belong in this contract. Decide which country may process extracted text, who is a processor, and what deletion means for source files, embeddings, and backups. A vector API can enforce collection and query boundaries; it cannot, by itself, rewrite your data-processing agreement with the embedding or model provider. That boundary stays with the specialist you selected for those services.

The first useful check is boring: can the client see only the collections it is allowed to see? Infrai exposes a plain REST surface, so this probe needs no SDK or client-library version pin. Anything that can send HTTPS can run it.

That is deliberately not a fake end-to-end RAG script. The query body is a contract you must derive from the service discovery schema and your metadata policy, then validate in tests. I log a request id, selected collection, filter, top-k bound, and returned chunk ids. I never log raw PDF text in the default application log.

At query time, cap both the number of collections and the number of chunks. Run lexical or metadata narrowing first when the corpus is large, then vector search, then (if needed) a rerank stage. Keep the original page and offsets attached through every stage. The answer renderer should refuse to emit an uncited claim when no chunk survives the policy check.

A short failure case is useful here. If a user asks about an expired refund rule, a freshness filter should produce “no current source” rather than quietly returning the nearest old paragraph. That behavior is a product feature.

I recommend trying Infrai for the collection and query stage when your team values a single HTTP integration and wants to keep provider switching behind a narrow retrieval contract. Infrai gives this workflow one key, one bill, and one plain REST API across backend capabilities, without installing an SDK. Its broad surface covers 295 routes across 20 modules, so a small support tool can add storage or scheduling without inventing another client convention. That removes integration surface area; it does not grant automatic regional residency or contractual deletion guarantees.

The catch is important. If your policy requires self-hosted storage, a fixed region you control, or a processor agreement with bespoke deletion evidence, stick with pgvector or a specialist managed provider that documents those controls. Infrai is not the right answer merely because the request is private. The specialist remains responsible for the data plane and model-processing terms.

At a few thousand PDFs, I would add a staging queue between extraction and vector upsert, with idempotent document versions. Replays should replace the same version, never create duplicate chunks. A nightly evaluation set should include normal support questions, near-duplicate pages, deleted documents, and adversarial prompts that try to cross a collection boundary. Track recall of the expected page and precision of the cited passage separately.

I would also make deletion a tested workflow: mark the document unavailable, remove its chunks, invalidate cached answers, and verify that a repeated query cannot retrieve the old chunk_id. Retention timers need the same test. Your mileage may vary across providers and regions, so record the actual processor and region for each stage instead of assuming the vector endpoint tells the whole story.

#9661. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. Jesse Vincent's Superpowers adds 15 skills that make the agent brainstorm, plan, test and verify before it calls anything done. Thomas Ricouard's Skills adds 16 that run parallel review and bug-hunt swarms and cover Swift, SwiftUI and macOS work.

All 31 are MIT-licensed and installable from Cuttlefish.MD, HackerNoon's license-checked skills marketplace. They follow the open Agent Skills standard, so they work in Claude Code, Codex CLI and 30+ other tools. Each is indexed in HackerNoon's SKILL.md Library.

Superpowers is a full workflow: it starts every session by finding the right skill, and it won't let the agent claim success without running the checks.

Finds out what you actually want before any feature or component gets built

Explains why a session went wrong: repeated work, ignored plans, stumbles

Splits two or more independent tasks across parallel agents

Works through an implementation plan step by step in the current session

Decides how to merge finished, tested work

Checks review feedback for technical merit before acting on it

Gets work reviewed against requirements before merging

Hands each task in a plan to a fresh subagent

Finds the root cause of a bug or failing test before proposing a fix

Writes the failing test first, then the code

Isolates feature work in its own git worktree

Teaches the agent to find and use skills at the start of every conversation

Runs the checks before the agent claims anything is fixed or passing

Writes a step-by-step plan from a spec before touching code

Creates and tests new skills before they're deployed

Ricouard's set runs read-only agent swarms for review and debugging, and goes deep on Swift, SwiftUI and macOS.

Writes App Store release notes from every user-facing change since the last tag

Runs parallel read-only agents to find a bug's root cause

Builds, runs and debugs the iOS project on a simulator with XcodeBuildMCP

Builds and reviews macOS menubar apps that use Tuist and SwiftUI

Scaffolds and packages SwiftPM macOS apps without an Xcode project

Plans and runs large refactors with parallel agents

Reviews past sessions and memory files to recommend the skills worth writing

Fixes slow renders, re-render thrash and laggy lists in React

Reviews a diff for reuse, quality and clarity, then simplifies it

Runs parallel read-only agents over a diff to catch regressions

Builds and reviews SwiftUI features with the iOS 26 Liquid Glass API

Audits and improves SwiftUI runtime performance

Example-driven patterns for SwiftUI views, navigation and modifiers

Refactors SwiftUI views into small subviews with MV-over-MVVM data flow

In Claude Code, add the marketplace and install the Dev Workflow plugin, which holds 28 of the 31. The last three sit in QA & Testing (test-driven-development), Writing & Blogging (writing-skills) and Design & UI (swiftui-ui-patterns).

For Codex CLI, Cursor or another agent that supports the standard, clone the repo and copy the skill folders you want into your agent's skills directory, such as .agents/skills/. Superpowers also ships its own marketplace from Jesse Vincent's repo.

Each skill keeps its MIT license and an ATTRIBUTION.md naming its author and source commit. Browse the full library at hackernoon.com/skills, and star Cuttlefish.MD on GitHub if these make your agent less reckless.

#9655. Web corporativa en 2026: diseñar impacto sin sacrificar rendimiento ni control

Posted on Nov 17 • Originally published at juliancardozo.github.io

Publicado originalmente en juliancardozo.github.io.

Una web corporativa ya no compite solo por informar qué hace una empresa. Compite por comunicar criterio, diferenciar una propuesta y conducir una conversación comercial. El reto técnico es lograr una experiencia memorable sin convertir la página en una SPA frágil, lenta o difícil de evolucionar. Pambú 2026 fue construido desde ese equilibrio.

Una visita institucional dura poco. En ese tiempo, la persona tiene que poder entender qué hace la organización, por qué debería prestarle atención y cuál es el siguiente paso. La arquitectura de información no puede ser una lista de secciones intercambiables: necesita una narrativa que ordene propuesta de valor, enfoque, identidad, servicios y contacto.

En Pambú 2026, la estructura se organiza como una experiencia de una página con navegación a secciones. El scroll deja de ser solo una forma de desplazarse y se convierte en el ritmo de la presentación. Para negocio, esto permite guiar el mensaje; para ingeniería, mantiene un modelo de contenido directo y comprensible.

El fondo animado con WebGL y Three.js incorpora profundidad y movimiento a una propuesta centrada en creatividad, tecnología e innovación. Pero el componente visual no puede cargar con el significado de la página. El contenido comercial, la navegación y el contacto deben permanecer disponibles como HTML semántico y legible sin depender de la capa gráfica.

Esta separación es un control de resiliencia. La experiencia enriquecida puede evolucionar, degradar de forma aceptable en hardware limitado o fallar sin bloquear el mensaje. El impacto visual es una capa de mejora progresiva, no una condición para que el sitio funcione.

GSAP y ScrollTrigger permiten sincronizar transiciones con la lectura de cada sección. Usarlos bien no significa animar todo: significa dirigir atención hacia un cambio de contexto, una jerarquía visual o una llamada a la acción. Cada animación debe justificar qué comprensión o conversión mejora.

En una página de alto impacto, el rendimiento es parte de la marca. El equipo debe tratar el peso de assets, el trabajo de renderizado y la ejecución en dispositivos de menor capacidad como restricciones de diseño. La elección de JavaScript vanilla para la capa de interacción reduce superficie de runtime y facilita que la experiencia se mantenga enfocada.

Pambú 2026 se implementa con HTML5, CSS3 y JavaScript vanilla, con Three.js y GSAP cargados desde CDN. Esta decisión no niega el valor de un framework; responde a un caso donde la página es una experiencia editorial acotada, no una aplicación con estados de negocio complejos.

La consecuencia es operativa: menos capas para desplegar, inspeccionar y modificar. El equipo puede concentrar su esfuerzo en narrativa, contenido, performance y calidad visual. Si el producto necesita luego CMS, personalización o funcionalidades transaccionales, la arquitectura puede crecer sobre una necesidad comprobada, no una hipótesis.

Principio de experiencia corporativa: el alto impacto surge cuando la narrativa, la identidad visual y el rendimiento trabajan como un sistema. La tecnología debe intensificar el mensaje, no convertirse en el mensaje.

#9652. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

#9651. Onboarding clínico: cómo evitar que un producto de salud empiece vacío

Posted on Nov 17 • Originally published at juliancardozo.github.io

Publicado originalmente en juliancardozo.github.io.

Milo Care nació de un problema de gestión de información: vacunas, medicación y controles repartidos entre una foto, un chat, una nota y la memoria. La primera decisión de producto fue evitar trasladar ese trabajo al usuario. Un onboarding útil no pide datos para llenar una base: transforma datos mínimos en un plan de cuidado accionable.

Un registro clínico que abre vacío le pide al usuario que reconstruya meses o años de información antes de obtener algo a cambio. Para un producto de cuidado, ese costo inicial compite directamente con el papel, el chat o la nota que ya usan. No es un detalle de UX: es un problema de activación y retención.

En Milo Care, el alta del perro captura país y datos relevantes para iniciar un calendario vacunal. El resultado esperado no es una ficha más completa; es una primera sesión que ya muestra próximas acciones, fechas y un historial sobre el que se puede operar.

El calendario no podía ser una lista genérica de vacunas. Las recomendaciones cambian por país, fuente y contexto clínico. La solución fue modelar reglas de negocio que distinguen el calendario de Argentina y Uruguay, con SENASA y las guías WSAVA como referencias, sin presentar la plataforma como sustituto de una indicación veterinaria.

Ese límite es parte de la arquitectura de dominio. El sistema puede organizar, recordar y mostrar el plan; la evaluación clínica y la decisión profesional siguen fuera del automatismo. Separar ambas responsabilidades evita que una recomendación de software se presente como diagnóstico.

El calendario inicial se integra con módulos de vacunas, medicamentos, citas y síntomas. Cada módulo maneja su propio estado y vencimiento, pero alimenta un único historial por animal. Esa consolidación permite que el dashboard priorice el trabajo pendiente y que los recordatorios operen sobre datos estructurados.

Para negocio, la decisión tiene un efecto claro: el producto entrega valor antes de pedir hábitos complejos. Para ingeniería, deja un dominio extensible para nuevas especies, clínicas veterinarias y planes premium sin convertir el onboarding en una colección de excepciones.

Principio de producto: el onboarding debe convertir la información mínima en una primera acción valiosa. En dominios de salud, las reglas automatizadas organizan el seguimiento, pero no reemplazan el criterio profesional.

#9648. NoisyTCP CVE-2026-99288: Pre-Authentication Remote DoS Causing Linux Kernel Panic via Crafted TCP Packets

NoisyTCP is a denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability that exploits a race condition between the lockless TCP socket lookup and socket reuse in the Linux kernel. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to trigger a NULL pointer dereference and a kernel panic using only crafted TCP traffic. TCP listeners with default configurations, including Nginx, Apache, and SSH, can be targeted, but the reproduction results demonstrated in public materials are limited to a remote DoS causing a host crash. The researcher stated that they created a highly restricted, lab-specific exploit for VMs, but did not demonstrate general-purpose remote code execution (RCE).

No additional hypotheses. Lab PoC success is not treated as confirmation of in-the-wild exploitation.

Linux web servers, SSH services, proxies, and container hosts are widely deployed, and application-level patches alone cannot remediate this issue. Inventory externally reachable listeners and kernel packages, and prioritize vendor fixes. Integrate availability monitoring, remote kernel logs, kdump, and load balancer health checks to ensure that host crashes lacking authentication logs can still be investigated as network-layer attacks.

#9645. How to Add Native Cross-Chain Swaps to a Wallet or App

AI, Web3, Cybersecurity, Startup Funding & Enterprise SaaS. Top Journalist, Analyst & Thought Leadership Media Leader.

AI, Web3, Cybersecurity, Startup Funding & Enterprise SaaS. Top Journalist, Analyst & Thought Leadership Media Leader.

AI, Web3, Cybersecurity, Startup Funding & Enterprise SaaS. Top Journalist, Analyst & Thought Leadership Media Leader.

For a multichain wallet, adding native cross-chain swaps is more than showing a conversion rate. Developers must obtain executable quotes, construct secure source-chain transactions, disclose fees, validate destinations and track settlement across two networks. Integrating an established decentralized exchange (DEX) can provide these capabilities without building independent cross-chain liquidity infrastructure.

THORChain is a decentralized cross-chain exchange (DEX) that enables swaps between supported native assets, including bitcoin (BTC) and ether (ETH). A wallet can request a quote, prepare a signed deposit from the user's wallet and monitor the outbound transfer. Users do not need to acquire RUNE separately for a standard supported BTC-to-ETH swap, although the network uses RUNE-paired liquidity internally. Integrators may configure affiliate fees for eligible transactions.

A user holding assets on multiple blockchains may otherwise move funds through a centralized exchange: deposit an asset, trade it, then withdraw to a different network. An in-wallet swap can reduce that friction and keep the transfer experience in the same product. For developers, however, the feature introduces new responsibilities around quoting, network support, transaction signing, status updates, failed transactions and refunds.

Native swaps deliver the actual destination-chain asset, rather than necessarily leaving the user with a wrapped representation. That can be valuable for users converting BTC into native ETH. But a native swap still depends on the settlement network while funds are moving; it is not the same as an instantaneous, risk-free transfer.

Direct network integration: public quote and status endpoints, no hosted partner key, maximum signing and routing control, and more implementation responsibility. Hosted aggregator API: partner x-api-key, managed eligible routes and fee configuration. Embeddable widget: partner setup and a ready-made swap interface. Third-party SDK: requirements vary by library, underlying route provider and version.

Developers can connect directly to THORChain's public quote and network-status interfaces without a hosted aggregator partner key. Their application must obtain a fresh quote, use the returned current inbound vault address and memo, construct the correct source-chain transaction and reconcile settlement status. Direct integration gives more control but leaves chain-specific signing, monitoring and recovery to the developer.

THORChain Swap offers a hosted aggregator, partner tooling and an embeddable widget. The aggregator at api.thorchain.org/v1 is separate from THORChain's public network interfaces: it requires an x-api-key issued through the affiliate program after review. Approved partners can configure relevant affiliate and service-fee arrangements, request available routes and review earnings. The widget can reduce interface development, but teams still need to test signing, availability, error handling and user support.

THORChain's Q3 2026 marketing update describes a hosted routing approach that prioritizes THORChain and may use Maya as an alternative where supported. Available providers and quotes can change; developers should verify the actual route, fees, network state and expected output instead of assuming that a listed option is executable or offers the best price.

SDKs and routing tools such as SwapKit may combine wallet handling with THORChain and other liquidity sources. They can reduce the amount of chain-specific work required, but teams should examine the exact supported providers, versions, API requirements and data-handling model. A wrapper library does not remove the need to implement transaction-state recovery, user notifications or security checks.

A practical choice depends on the product. An existing wallet with mature chain-signing support may prefer direct integration. A website adding swaps for the first time may prefer the hosted widget. A multichain application comparing several liquidity networks may benefit from an SDK or aggregator, provided it understands how routes are selected.

The app requests a quote for the source asset, destination asset, amount and destination address. Where appropriate, it includes affiliate information and slippage settings. The quote provides an estimated output, itemized fees, an inbound address, a memo or other chain-specific instructions, and an expiry. THORChain's published quickstart uses normalized asset identifiers such as BTC.BTC and ETH.ETH and represents values in 1e8 base units for its quote examples; production integrations must follow the chosen endpoint's exact schema.

The wallet constructs and signs a transaction on the source chain. For a standard memo-based flow, the deposit must reach the correct current inbound vault and carry the specified memo. The app should never substitute a hardcoded vault address or silently change the destination. The user signs with their own wallet; the integrating app should not collect or store their private keys.

After the inbound transaction is confirmed and observed, THORChain executes the swap using liquidity in its supported pools and sends the output asset on the destination chain. A quote is indicative rather than a guarantee of immediate settlement: source confirmations, outbound scheduling, liquidity conditions and network pauses can affect timing and completion.

The app should distinguish deposit broadcast, source confirmation, network observation, swap execution, outbound initiation and destination confirmation. THORNode transaction status and Midgard actions can help reconcile these stages. THORChain Swap's hosted developer documentation states that it does not emit webhooks, so a reliable application may need polling and durable transaction-state recovery. A source-chain confirmation alone is not evidence that the destination asset has arrived.

THORChain supports affiliate fees on eligible swaps. Its native quote documentation permits affiliate fees from 0 to 1,000 basis points: 100 basis points is 1%, and 1,000 is 10%. A valid RUNE address or correctly configured THORName can identify an affiliate. Invalid or expired identifiers can cause fees to be skipped. Multiple affiliate recipients may be configured within the network's applicable overall limits.

Fee revenue is conditional on completed, eligible volume and the applicable fee arrangement. It is not guaranteed profit: high fees reduce the amount users receive and may make a quote less competitive. Integrators should disclose their fees clearly, compare net execution outcomes and understand whether their chosen aggregator shares revenue among multiple providers or services.

For example, a 30-basis-point affiliate fee is 0.30% of the applicable calculation base, not $0.30 per swap. Actual credited amounts depend on conversion and settlement rules. Show users the estimated destination amount after visible fees, rather than emphasizing only the partner's fee percentage.

The full cost of a native swap can include the source-chain network fee, liquidity-related swap fee, destination-chain outbound fee and any affiliate or interface fee. Costs change with congestion, liquidity depth and trade size. The most useful comparison is the estimated net amount delivered to the destination wallet, not one advertised fee in isolation.

THORChain also provides streaming swaps, which split eligible transactions into multiple sub-swaps over time to reduce price impact for larger orders. Streaming does not guarantee the best price or the fastest completion. Wallet interfaces should explain the potential timing trade-off and show realistic output estimates and limits.

Before production, test a small supported end-to-end swap and its refund path where practical. Validate address formats, precision, memo limits, quote expiry, current vault addresses, minimum amounts and EVM destination restrictions. Record source and destination transaction IDs and reconcile them after restarts. Do not expose a chain or asset pair as live based only on documentation: request a current executable quote.

Quote values and inbound addresses are time-sensitive, and network vault configurations can change. Fetch or validate a fresh quote before a user signs, honor its expiry and follow chain-specific memo instructions. An outdated inbound address or malformed memo may delay a transaction or change its refund behavior.

Check live pool and chain status before displaying an executable route. Persist transaction identifiers and state so a restart does not lose a pending swap. Handle delays, outbound failures and refunds when THORChain or another connected chain pauses, without promising an unsupported recovery time.

The source and destination networks may use different address encodings, precision and memo behavior. Validate destination formats, quote units, dust thresholds and minimum amounts. Present a clear confirmation screen showing exactly what users send and expect to receive; do not let a chain mismatch become an irreversible loss.

Show estimated net output, applicable fees, price impact and whether streaming execution is enabled. Give users separate broadcast, observed, pending payout, completed and refunded states. A small end-to-end test may reveal integration problems but cannot eliminate trading, network or operational risk.

THORChain's published ecosystem information includes Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Base, XRP Ledger, TRON, Dogecoin, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Cosmos, Solana and Zcash among its supported networks. Developers should check live chain and pool status, the exact available asset pair and current documentation before claiming a route is available. A chain being listed does not mean every token on it or every conversion path is operational.

Not for direct integration through THORChain's public interfaces. The separate hosted THORChain Swap aggregator API requires a partner key issued after affiliate-program review.

No. In a typical self-custody integration, users authorize a source-chain deposit from their own wallet and receive native output at the selected destination. During the exchange, assets pass through THORChain's vault and validator system; self-custody at signing does not mean the transfer is instantaneous or without risk.

Potentially. Integrators can configure eligible affiliate fees, and revenue depends on completed swap volume, the fee arrangement and the underlying network mechanism. Neither revenue nor profitability is guaranteed.

No. RUNE functions within THORChain's liquidity pools. A user can send a supported source asset and receive the supported destination asset without separately buying RUNE.

Yes, for eligible routes. THORChain supports streaming swaps, which divide an order into sub-swaps to manage price impact. Integrators should explain the possible additional waiting time and monitor all legs until final settlement.

THORChain Swap documents an alternative memoless flow for certain eligible transactions. Route availability and requirements must be checked at the time of use. Users still authorize and send assets, and developers must verify current instructions, quote conditions and destination addresses.

Adding native cross-chain swaps requires accurate quotes, chain-correct signing, transparent fees, live route checks and dependable settlement tracking. THORChain's decentralized exchange infrastructure and separate hosted aggregator tools give developers a choice between more implementation control and faster integration.

The central product decision is where the developer wants to own complexity: wallet signing, routing, quote presentation, affiliate fees or user-support workflows. Whichever integration path is chosen, the user should be able to understand what they are sending, what they may receive and what happens if the transaction does not settle as expected.

Information checked November 12, 2026. Network support, routes, API requirements and fee terms can change. Developers should validate live conditions and current documentation before release. This article is educational, not financial advice.

#9643. exploit_agent: Automating Everything from Patch Diff Analysis to Exploit Generation and Execution Without Human-in-the-Loop

GTIG identified a multi-agent framework named exploit_agent operating on a public staging server. The framework continuously compares web application code before and after patches, analyzes potential vulnerabilities, creates exploits, and automatically executes them against targets without human-in-the-loop intervention. The server also contained data gathered from victims, along with scripts for internal reconnaissance, brute force, and web shell deployment.

Confirmed Related Capabilities: GTIG identified scripts on the staging server capable of supporting internal reconnaissance, brute force, web shell deployment, and the removal of other attackers' web shells. Execution methods and sequences within individual victim environments have not been publicly disclosed.

Inference: The following items are candidates for investigation. An attacker's use of external LLMs or retrieval of public source code may not leave traces in victim-side logs. Access to source repositories and CI artifacts should be verified using audit logs restricted to organization-managed assets.

No additional hypotheses. Do not assert victim counts, attribution, or exploit success rates beyond publicly available information.

Because PentAGI activity targeting Asia has been confirmed, organizations should treat internet-facing CMS platforms, plugins, and business applications as priority assets. Operating under the assumption that the window between patch diff publication and exploitation is compressed, organizations should combine rapid patching, virtual patching, web process monitoring, outbound traffic restrictions, and source or CI artifact access auditing.

#9642. How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later.

The bakers of King Arthur are here to solve the kitchen conundrums you share with us, whether it’s on the phone, computer, or by the good old postal service. In Ask the Baker’s Hotline, Annabelle will pick the brains of the talented King Arthur Baker’s Hotline team to tackle some of your most-asked questions.

Ryan from our Baker’s Hotline is here with the answer.

You sure can! It will still work the next time you want to bake. But remember, as with any dairy product, there are always precautions to take.

The USDA recommends keeping butter at room temperature for no more than two days to prevent spoilage. Salt is a preservative and can lengthen the shelf life, but for the sake of this article, we’re talking about unsalted butter. (It’s more appropriate for baking and is the type called for in most King Arthur recipes.)

“If the butter has only been on the counter at room temperature for a few hours or overnight and has maintained a temperature below 70°F, it should be just fine to place back in the fridge,” says Ryan. “You may not notice a difference in the performance of the butter when you eventually use it, other than the wrapper being a bit wet or soft. Food safety-wise, it’s still good to use.”

“If the butter became very soft or started to melt during its time on the counter (or in the microwave if you were speeding up the process), you can put it back in the fridge, but it may not be the best to use in your recipe,” Ryan suggests. “You may notice when it solidifies that it’s separated or grainy. The water, fats, and solids in butter are an emulsion, which can break when melted and re-solidified.” If your recipe depends on butter to create air or structure, like a cake that calls for creaming butter and sugar, you’ll want to start over with new butter.

“If you used that butter in a recipe requiring creaming, the air you incorporate wouldn’t be as stable since the structure of the butter has changed,” Ryan says. “Your baked goods may not rise properly, and frostings may be soft and loose. Is it still safe to use? Food safety-wise, yes. But structure-wise, perhaps not.”

That butter can still be used for other things though! Extra-softened or even melted and re-solidified butter will still work perfectly to spread on toast or pancakes, to be made into brown butter, or to remelt and use in recipes calling for melted butter like a Graham Cracker Crust.

If your butter has been unrefrigerated for more than two days, you run the risk of it going rancid. As Ryan says, “There is no coming back from rancid butter.” It has a distinctly unpleasant flavor and a noticeable rancid smell that carries over into baked goods. It’s best to dispose of the butter if this happens.

But what if you want to keep your butter at room temperature for days at a time to slather on your morning toast? Ryan recommends storing your butter in a butter keeper if you want to leave it on the counter. “The water in the base of the jar creates an airtight seal, helping prevent the butter from spoiling. So long as it is stored away from direct heat and light, the butter in a container like this will be fine for a few days. Be sure to replace the water often and clean the container before filling again.”

“When working with butter in a recipe, I like to bring out and soften only the amount that is needed for what I am working on. That way, I don’t end up with extra butter that won’t be used right away,” he says. “Repeatedly moving butter from the fridge to the counter and then back invites spoilage and poor performance.”

In a rush? To soften your butter more quickly, Ryan advises, “Cut your butter into pats and place them on a plate in a single layer at room temperature. More surface area means that the butter will soften a bit faster!”

#9640. Map It Before You Automate It: 10 Best Practices for Business Process Automation

Researching and learning new things and improving my skills

Researching and learning new things and improving my skills

Researching and learning new things and improving my skills

Business processes will include several different tasks, departments and systems. This can become time consuming and cumbersome to manage manually and can cause delays, double work, miscommunication and human error. Understand your current processes, identify where improvements can be made and implement automation in a structured way. By mapping out each step of the process, your business can be more organized, dependable and efficient.

Whether you’re looking to automate customer queries, payments, employee records or general internal processes, having a plan in place can help reduce manual work and improve consistency.

Business process automation mapping is when you produce a visual representation of your business processes so you can identify which parts can be automated.

When combined, this gives your organization a greater understanding of their processes and where automation can be most beneficial.

Before beginning to automate your processes, it is important to understand your current operations. If you try to automate an inefficient process without taking a look at the structure, you could just speed up your problems.

Creating a dependable automation strategy requires more than just choosing the right software and linking your systems together. First you need to understand what your business needs from its processes.

To help improve your processes and make them more efficient, there are some best practice tips to consider:

The first thing to do is understand what areas within your business processes are taking too long or requiring too much manual work.

Speak to your employees who regularly carry out these tasks. They can give you real insight into any issues.

By knowing what the issue actually is, you won’t waste time automating processes which don’t need much changes.

Each process map should be created with a clear objective. This means understanding what you want to achieve. You may want to reduce the time taken to process invoices, improve customer onboarding or make it easier to approve employee leave.

By identifying clear start and end points, you will avoid any unnecessary tasks.

Being clear with your scope will also help you know which departments, employees, systems and resources are involved.

One of the most important things you can do is document your current process. Make sure you document each task in the order it happens including decisions, approval, handover and exceptions.

Your basic process map could look like: Start of task->Gathering information->Verifying data->Approval/decision making->End of task-> Keeping records.

By documenting your current processes, you can identify any unnecessary tasks and understand how information flows between departments.

You’ll also have a reference point to compare your original process to your improved automated process.

Not every task in your business will be suitable for automation. Focus on processes with predictable patterns and repeated tasks.

Some examples could be: Sending confirmation emails, Creating invoices, Updating customer information, Scheduling regular notifications, Processing standard application forms, Organizing & transferring business data.

Jobs which require complex decision making, negotiating or personal interaction may still need human input. Starting with simpler processes will help you understand how the technology works and identify any issues.

Although you are automating processes, you will still need human oversight. Make sure your employees understand what tasks have been automated.

A well planned process map should help you to understand:

By knowing who has responsibility, you will avoid confusion and know who to refer to if there are any issues.

Your process map should be easy to understand for everyone in your department.

Use the same icons, labels and layout when mapping your processes. Different methods such as flowcharts and swim lanes can help you map different types of processes.

Swim lanes are great to use if you have multiple departments involved as it shows you who is responsible for each task.

Ensure you are not providing too much information. Too much can make it confusing. However, keep it simple and you may miss out on important decisions and responsibilities.

Many businesses will have multiple systems and databases. However, to make your automation more effective, you need to ensure accurate communication between systems.

Before implementing your automated process, look at the systems you need to use and see if they can communicate with each other.

If the systems aren’t integrated correctly, your employees may still have to manually transfer information. Consider the compatibility of your systems, accuracy of data, permissions and integration.

Testing your process is important to ensure it works how it should. Before implementing your automation throughout your organization, test your process in realistic scenarios.

Gather feedback from employees who regularly use the process and make any adjustments.

Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are written instructions for carrying out specific tasks. This is important to ensure consistency.

Having everything documented will help new employees understand the process and reduce reliance on verbal instructions.

As your business introduces new technology, grows or changes internal responsibilities your processes will change. Process mapping shouldn’t be a one-off task.

Regularly review your automated processes and measure how they are performing using metrics such as:

This will help you understand if your automation is improving as expected.

Whilst efficiency is important, your automated processes should be reliable. Consider the following best practices:

Following these best practices will help you to keep your processes consistent and adapt to your changing requirements.

Business process automation mapping is an important part of improving your modern business. It will help you understand your current processes, identify any inefficiencies and identify where automation can help.

Following best practices will help you clearly define responsibilities, keep processes consistent, improve integration and reduce any unnecessary manual work. However, you will need to continually focus on your processes. Test your processes, provide the right guidance and keep your process maps updated.

By using effective process mapping, careful planning and regular monitoring, you can create more reliable processes, improve productivity and create a strong base for your long term growth.

#9638. null becomes mixed on the PHP DTO

I pasted nulls as property values and expected the same type everywhere. On the JSON converter they stay null in the paste, but the drafts diverge. Conversion runs in the browser. Nothing is uploaded.

Laravel writes null for each key. TypeScript types each field as null. The PHP DTO types each property as mixed. CSV writes the headers name,age,meta with an empty row underneath.

That is different from a nested object. When meta is {"active":true}, TypeScript drafts interface Meta and the PHP DTO still uses public array $meta. A null meta does not create that nest. It is mixed on the PHP class and null in TypeScript.

A missing key on the PHP DTO is still assigned with ?? null, including on a property declared public int $id. That is an assignment fallback. A JSON null value is an explicit null in the paste, and the draft types that property as mixed on the PHP class.

The class name stays DataTransferObject. Rename it before the draft ships.

A trailing comma such as {"a":1,} clears every format with Expected double-quoted property name in JSON at position 7 (line 1 column 8). That is not a null. Repair broken text in the JSON formatter, then convert again.

Guide: https://kepttools.com/guides/json-to-typescript-php-dto-laravel

#9637. Leaked Credentials Are an Enterprise Problem: GitGuardian Extends Its Good Samaritan Program

The world's leading cybersecurity press release distribution platform.

The world's leading cybersecurity press release distribution platform.

The world's leading cybersecurity press release distribution platform.

New York, USA, November 16th, 2026/CyberNewswire/--AI attribution has linked more than 3,913 high-impact leaks to 1,532 companies since spring; security experts handle critical disclosures to enterprise security teams.

GitGuardian, the secrets security platform, today announced the Enterprise Good Samaritan Program, an expansion of its longstanding responsible disclosure efforts aimed at strengthening security across the broader digital ecosystem.

Combining AI-powered attribution with expert security analysis, the program identifies high-impact credential leaks that could give attackers a path into an organization's systems or data. It traces these exposures to affected companies and delivers actionable disclosures to their security teams, showing how an attacker could exploit the credentials and what they could gain access to. For the first time, GitGuardian can extend these warnings to any company in the world, regardless of its size or whether it's a GitGuardian customer.

Since 2018, GitGuardian's original Good Samaritan Program has detected more than 83 million exposed secrets on public GitHub, sending 11.9 million alerts to 5.9 million developers. But notifying a developer doesn't necessarily lead to revocation. Approximately 90% of valid secrets remain unrevoked a week after the developer responsible for the leak has been alerted.

To date, the Enterprise Good Samaritan Program has linked more than 3,913 high-impact leaks to 1,532 companies. GitGuardian followed up with them, typically reaching at least five people at each organization.

The scale of the problem is growing. GitGuardian's 2026 State of Secrets Sprawl report found that 28.65 million new secrets were exposed on public GitHub in 2025, a 34% year-over-year increase. The Enterprise Good Samaritan Program gets exposed credentials to the security teams that can revoke them.

"For years, we've warned developers, but they're not always the ones who can revoke it. Our expertise combined with AI now helps us identify at scale the organizations behind serious exposures at scale, and our researchers work to reach the people who can respond. Attackers now have the ability, with AI offensive harnesses like ARTEX, to use these credentials to target companies at scale. Those companies deserve to know, whether they're our customers or not. And if a company has no clear way to receive a warning, the warning doesn’t help. Every company needs a door for these reports, and someone behind it.” — Eric Fourrier, CEO at GitGuardian

The Enterprise Good Samaritan Program combines continuous public monitoring, AI-assisted analysis, and human-led disclosure to identify serious credential exposures and help organizations respond.

GitGuardian monitors public sources, including GitHub and Docker Hub, for exposed credentials. Its AI agents now screen more than 1 million public incidents each month and investigate over 100,000 in depth, helping identify the affected organizations and assess the potential impact of exposure, including credential validity, permissions, and the systems or data at risk.

Human experts review high-impact findings before disclosure, providing the affected organization with the context needed to investigate and remediate the exposure. Rather than relying exclusively on notifications to individual developers, GitGuardian contacts multiple people within affected organizations, works to reach the relevant security teams, and escalates manually when automated outreach goes unanswered.

The value of this escalation was demonstrated in May 2026, when GitGuardian researchers identified a public GitHub repository containing sensitive CISA-related data and valid cloud credentials. Nine automated alerts had failed to resolve the exposure. After GitGuardian researchers escalated through CERT/CC and established contacts, the repository was taken offline within 26 hours of human escalation.

The need for timely disclosure is becoming more urgent as attackers automate credential discovery and exploitation. In November 2026, Microsoft documented attackers using agentic AI to search public GitHub repositories for exposed credentials. In one observed case, an AI agent went from searching for a leaked secret to extracting data from Azure Key Vault in five minutes.

The speed of these attacks makes unresolved credential exposures especially dangerous, and reinforces the need for organizations to have a reliable way to receive and act on external security disclosures.

With only 35% of contacted organizations responding to the program’s outreach, GitGuardian is calling on companies to establish clear, monitored channels for receiving security disclosures from external researchers, such as a security.txt file and a staffed security inbox.

The Enterprise Good Samaritan Program operates under GitGuardian's published disclosure principles, which emphasize timely notification, non-destructive verification, transparency, traceable research activity, and persistent follow-up.

Organizations receive the full details of their exposures without needing to sign up or become customers.

To learn more about the Enterprise Good Samaritan Program and GitGuardian's responsible disclosure principles, visit GitGuardian's Enterprise Good Samaritan Program Page. Organizations can also assess their exposure on public GitHub using GitGuardian's GitHub Security Audit.

GitGuardian is the secrets security platform built to protect the credentials that let code, machines, and AI agents access critical systems. The platform helps organizations detect exposed credentials across code, endpoints, and public sources; remediate incidents at scale with identity context, risk prioritization, and guided workflows; and prevent new leaks with security controls embedded in developer and AI coding workflows.

More than 600,000 developers worldwide trust GitGuardian. Enterprise customers include DigitalOcean, ING, BASF, Datadog, Euronext, and Bouygues Telecom.

For more information, visit the GitGuardian website.

#9635. What is piloncillo? This sweetener makes great cookies, pan dulce, and more: Use this traditional Mexican unrefined sugar for a dash of flavor and history.

This article is part of our feature celebrating Pan Dulce. Find all things pan dulce here.

Categorically, piloncillo is a “non-centrifugal” cane sugar, meaning it is an unrefined sugar product and a true natural brown sugar. It’s mostly consumed in Mexico and Latin America, but a similar product can be found in Asia, known as jaggery in India. Though often lumped together, these unrefined dark sugars are very different from brown sugars on the market today, which have been refined to a large degree — in some cases, they’re actually just white sugar with coloring or molasses added.

Making piloncillo, on the other hand, involves an artisanal process that’s hundreds of years old. To make it, pressed cane juice is boiled to evaporate the water and deeply caramelize the sugar. The cooked cane is then poured into molds (often made of wood) and left to dry and harden. Traditional piloncillo is conical in shape and can vary in size from small to large cones but is most commonly found in a medium size that weighs about 200 grams. In Guatemala and Colombia, it is called panela, where it is cooked to a lighter degree and typically formed into a brick, rather than cone, shape. Other forms of piloncillo can be granulated or liquid (which is more rare).

Minimally processed and boldly flavored, piloncillo was historically a prized and respected foodstuff. As an unrefined cane sugar, piloncillo provides more complex vitamins and minerals than refined sugars, which undergo processing and whitening methods that also strip nutrients from the whole food. And piloncillo is also great for baking, providing notes of burnt caramel and hints of smoke. Plus, its rich molasses qualities keep baked goods moist and fresh for longer.

Always look at the ingredient label when purchasing piloncillo and make sure it says 100% pure cane juice or cane sugar. It is becoming increasingly common to find imitation products marketed as jaggery or piloncillo that contain coloring and corn syrup. You can find good piloncillo at specialty grocery stores or online at retailers.

In Mexico and throughout Latin America, piloncillo is an important ingredient in many traditional dishes. (Some will even say it’s not the “real dish” if you substitute sugar in these recipes due to the deep flavors and richness that only piloncillo can provide.) This deep, dark unrefined sugar lends its characteristic flavor and texture to popular foods and beverages such as capirotada, tepache, coyotas, atole, café de olla, calabaza al horno, coricos, and hojarascas, to name a few!

I love adding piloncillo when I’m making champurrado. In this warm and thick chocolate beverage, the piloncillo is chopped or grated and dissolved in the pot with water or milk before adding the chocolate and masa. In this recipe, the piloncillo’s intense sweet and smoky flavors pair well with the chocolate and corn masa.

While there are many dishes and uses for piloncillo, it’s not a simple substitution for granulated white sugar in recipes, but you can use it the same as you would brown sugar with a 1:1 substitution by weight.  Depending on how hard the cone is, it can be crumbled or grated for easier measuring. If it is very hard, try cutting it in half with a sharp knife and then placing it between parchment paper or a towel and beating with a rolling pin.
